intro: A father dissolves salt in water. A boy waits three nights at Death's door. A woman scholar stands up in a king's court and will not stop asking. These scenes come from the Upanishads, the last layer of the Vedas, which scholars date from about 800 BCE onward.

In this unit you will learn the two great words of the Upanishads: atman, the self, and Brahman, ultimate reality. You will read famous lines such as 'That art thou' (Chandogya 6.8.7) and 'Lead me from the unreal to the real' (Brihadaranyaka 1.3.28). You will see how Shankara, Ramanuja and Madhva read the same words in different ways.

Then you will meet the people in the stories: Nachiketa, Svetaketu, Satyakama, Gargi and Maitreyi. By the end, you will be able to explain key ideas, cite passages and describe how different Hindu schools read them.
bigQuestion: What do the Upanishads teach about the self and reality, and why do they teach it through questions?

words.d: a Vedic text of teachings about the self and ultimate reality
ultimate reality, the ground of everything
'end of the Veda'; the Upanishads and schools built on them
Shankara's school: atman and Brahman are not two
Ramanuja's school: souls are real parts of God's body
Madhva's school: God and souls are forever distinct
'not this, not this'; Brahman is beyond description
lord of death, Nachiketa's teacher in the Katha Upanishad
the good, as opposed to the merely pleasant
a careful search for knowledge by asking questions

test.q: Where does 'That art thou' first appear?
test.why: Tat tvam asi first appears at Chandogya 6.8.7.

choices: Lead me from the unreal to the real
test.why: Brihadaranyaka 1.3.28 is 'Lead me from the unreal to the real'.

test.q: What does Nachiketa ask as his third wish?
test.why: Nachiketa asks Yama about what happens after death.

test.q: In the salt lesson, what does Svetaketu find?
test.why: The salt cannot be seen but is tasted everywhere.

test.q: Who compared her questions to two sharp arrows?
test.why: Gargi likens her two questions to arrows.

test.q: Who translated the Upanishads in SBE 1 and 15?
test.why: Max Müller translated them in 1879 and 1884.

test.q: What does the chariot image teach?
test.why: The Katha uses the chariot to teach self-control.

test.q: What date do scholars give the oldest Upanishads?
test.why: Scholars date the oldest to about 800–500 BCE.

test.q: Who had the Upanishads translated into Persian?
test.why: Dara Shikoh sponsored the 1657 Persian translation.
Maitreyi asks whether wealth can make her immortal.

test.q: Who taught that God and souls are forever distinct?

write.prompt: What does 'That art thou' mean? Cite Chandogya 6.8.7 and one other passage (Müller, SBE 1 or 15). Explain what the text says and how Shankara and Ramanuja or Madhva read it.
tips: Name the Upanishad, chapter and verse, and Müller's translation.
Say whose reading you are describing: "Shankara reads..."
Compare readings without saying one is right.
Use terms like atman, Brahman, Advaita and Dvaita.
